claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 15 years old - his birthday was earlier this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 15 years old and had his birthday earlier this year.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just to clarify further:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status (or pre-settled status) in the UK under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Do you currently have responsibility for Alex - meaning you are providing day-to-day care and he lives with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives at home with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you currently receiving any other benefits such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, or Pension Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

**What is your current residential status - do you live in England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more question to complete my assessment:

**Are there any circumstances where Alex might be considered a "qualifying young person" - for example, is he registered with a careers service, or is he waiting to start education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not registered with any careers service or waiting to start any education or training.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have sufficient details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key facts:
- Alex is 15 years old and had his birthday earlier this year
- He is not in full-time education or training
- He is not registered with a careers service or waiting to start education or training
- You are a British citizen with responsibility for Alex
- You live in England
- You are not receiving other means-tested benefits

Based on UK Child Benefit rules, eligibility requires that the child is under 16 years old, or under 19 and in full-time education or training (or a "qualifying young person"). Since Alex is 15, he meets the age requirement. However, the critical issue is that Alex is no longer in full-time education or training and is not a qualifying young person, which means he would not be eligible after reaching the upper age threshold that applies to non-students.

Let me make my formal determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 

Child Benefit is available for children under 16 years old, and can continue for young people aged 16-19 if they are in full-time education or training, or if they are registered as a "qualifying young person" with a careers service. Since Alex is 15 but is not in full-time education or training and is not a qualifying young person, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

If Alex's circumstances change and he enters full-time education or training, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him again at that point.

reasonings: Alex is 15 years old. While Child Benefit is available for children under 16 years old automatically, Alex is no longer in full-time education or training and is not registered as a qualifying young person with a careers service. Child Benefit continues beyond age 16 only if the young person is in full-time education or training, or is a qualifying young person. Since Alex does not meet these criteria, he does not qualify for Child Benefit.
